steps.text: Assalamu alaikum, my student. Letters are only half of reading. The other half is the small marks that tell your mouth which sound to make. The first is the fatha: a small slanted stroke above a letter. It gives the short sound 'a', as in 'cat'.

steps.note: Ba with a fatha on top: say 'ba'.
Ta with a fatha: 'ta'.
Seen with a fatha: 'sa'.
Seen in the Qur'an at 2:29. Every letter here carries a fatha, so each is read with 'a'.

steps.question: How do you read the letter ك with a fatha above it?
steps.why: A fatha above a letter gives the short 'a': ka.

steps.question: Where does the fatha sit?
steps.why: The fatha is a small slanted stroke written above the letter.

steps.text: Well walked. Come back to this lesson whenever it feels shaky - Wasia is proud of you.
Assalamu alaikum, my student. The second mark is the kasra: the same small slanted stroke, but written below the letter. It gives the short sound 'i', as in 'sit'.

steps.note: Ba with a kasra under it: 'bi'.
Ta with a kasra: 'ti'.
Meem with a kasra: 'mi'.
Seen in the Qur'an at 2:154. The first letter carries a kasra: 'li'. The next two carry fathas.

steps.question: How do you read ن with a kasra under it?
steps.why: A kasra below a letter gives the short 'i': ni.

steps.question: What is the difference between fatha and kasra?
options: Fatha is above and says 'a'; kasra is below and says 'i'
Fatha is below and says 'i'; kasra is above and says 'a'
steps.why: Fatha sits above and sounds 'a'. Kasra sits below and sounds 'i'.

steps.text: Well walked. Come back to this lesson whenever it feels shaky - Wasia is proud of you.
Assalamu alaikum, my student. The third mark is the damma: a small curl, like a tiny waw, written above the letter. It gives the short sound 'u', as in 'put'.

steps.note: Ba with a damma: 'bu'.
Kaf with a damma: 'ku'.
Lam with a damma: 'lu'.
Seen in the Qur'an at 2:178. Three letters, three marks: damma 'ku', kasra 'ti', fatha 'ba'.

steps.question: How do you read م with a damma above it?
steps.why: A damma gives the short 'u': mu.

steps.question: Read the word: كُتِبَ
steps.why: Damma then kasra then fatha: ku-ti-ba.

steps.text: Well walked. Come back to this lesson whenever it feels shaky - Wasia is proud of you.

lessons.title: Lesson 32: Long vowels - alif, waw, ya

steps.text: Assalamu alaikum, my student. A short vowel can be stretched into a long one. A fatha followed by an alif gives 'aa'. A kasra followed by a ya gives 'ii'. A damma followed by a waw gives 'uu'. Hold the sound for about two beats.

steps.note: Fatha plus alif: a long 'aa'.
Kasra plus ya: a long 'ii'.
Damma plus waw: a long 'uu'.

steps.question: Which letter stretches a fatha into a long 'aa'?
steps.why: Alif after a fatha makes 'aa'.

steps.question: Which letter stretches a damma into a long 'uu'?
steps.why: Waw after a damma makes 'uu'.

steps.question: How do you read كِي?
steps.why: Kasra plus ya: a long 'ii', so kii.

steps.text: Well walked. Come back to this lesson whenever it feels shaky - Wasia is proud of you.

lessons.title: Lesson 33: Sukun - a letter with no vowel

steps.text: Assalamu alaikum, my student. Sometimes a letter carries no vowel at all. A small circle above it, the sukun, tells you to stop on the sound and let the next letter follow straight away. In many printed Mushafs it is drawn as a small head-shaped mark; the idea is the same.

steps.note: Ba with a sukun: just 'b', with no vowel after it.
A fatha-letter followed by a sukun-letter: 'ab'.
Seen in the Qur'an at 2:80. The lam has a sukun, so the word stops on 'l'.
Seen in the Qur'an at 2:210. Again the lam stops: 'hal'.
Seen in the Qur'an at 2:74. The nun stops: 'min'.

steps.question: What does a sukun tell you?
steps.why: Sukun means the letter is read without a vowel.

steps.question: How do you read the word هَلۡ?
steps.why: The lam carries a sukun, so it is just 'l': hal.

steps.text: Well walked. Come back to this lesson whenever it feels shaky - Wasia is proud of you.

Assalamu alaikum, my student. A small mark shaped like a tiny sin, the shaddah, written above a letter means that letter is doubled: you press it once to end one sound and again to start the next. It is read as if the letter were written twice, the first with a sukun.

steps.note: Ba doubled with a fatha: 'b-ba'.
Seen in the Qur'an at 2:28. The meem is doubled: 'thum-ma'.
Seen in the Qur'an at 1:2. The ba is doubled: 'rab-bi'.
Seen in the Qur'an at 2:20. The lam is doubled: 'kul-li'.
Seen in the Qur'an at 2:121. The qaf is doubled: 'haq-qa'.

steps.question: What does a shaddah mean?
steps.why: A shaddah doubles the letter it sits on.

steps.question: How many sounds does رَبِّ have when the ba is doubled?
steps.why: The doubled ba is pressed twice: rab-bi.

steps.text: Well walked. Come back to this lesson whenever it feels shaky - Wasia is proud of you.

lessons.title: Lesson 35: Tanween - the 'n' at the end

steps.text: Assalamu alaikum, my student. Doubling the vowel mark at the end of a word gives tanween: a short vowel followed by an 'n' sound that is not written as a letter. Two fathas give 'an'. Two kasras give 'in'. Two dammas give 'un'. Tanween only ever appears at the end of a word.

steps.note: Two fathas: the ending 'an'. (With this mark an alif is usually written after the letter.)
Two kasras: the ending 'in'.
Two dammas: the ending 'un'.
Seen in the Qur'an at 11:12. Two dammas at the end: 'kanzun'.
Seen in the Qur'an at 10:61. Two kasras at the end: 'amalin'.
Seen in the Qur'an at 23:38. Two dammas at the end: 'rajulun'.

steps.question: Two kasras under the last letter give which ending?
steps.why: Two kasras give the ending 'in'.

steps.question: Where does tanween appear?
options: Only at the end of a word
Only at the start of a word
steps.why: Tanween is only written on the last letter of a word.

steps.text: Well walked. Come back to this lesson whenever it feels shaky - Wasia is proud of you.
Assalamu alaikum, my student. Now put it together. Read each letter, then its mark, left to right in your mind but right to left on the page. Read slowly first; speed comes by itself.

steps.note: Seen in the Qur'an at 2:29. Fatha, fatha, fatha.
Seen in the Qur'an at 2:60. A fatha, then a sukun: 'qad'.
Seen in the Qur'an at 2:28. A damma, then a doubled meem with a fatha.
Seen in the Qur'an at 96:2. Fatha, fatha, then tanween 'in'.

steps.question: Read the word: بَلۡ
steps.why: Fatha then a lam with sukun: bal.

steps.question: Read the word: كَذَّبَ
steps.why: The dhal carries a shaddah, so it is doubled: kadh-dha-ba.

steps.text: Well walked. Come back to this lesson whenever it feels shaky - Wasia is proud of you.

Assalamu alaikum, my student. In Arabic writing, most letters join to the letter that follows them. Because of that, a letter can look slightly different at the start of a word, in the middle, at the end, or when it stands alone. The core of the shape stays the same; look for the body and the dots.

steps.note: Ba alone.
Ba at the start of a word: the body is shortened and it reaches toward the next letter.
Ba in the middle: it joins on both sides.
Ba at the end: it joins from the right and ends with its full tail.

steps.question: Why can a letter look different in a word?
options: Because it joins to its neighbours
Because it is a different letter
steps.why: Letters join to their neighbours, so their shape adapts by position.

steps.question: What stays the same in every shape of ب?
options: The dot below and the body
steps.why: The body and the single dot below stay recognisable.

steps.text: Well walked. Come back to this lesson whenever it feels shaky - Wasia is proud of you.

lessons.title: Lesson 38: Six letters that do not join forward

steps.text: Assalamu alaikum, my student. Six letters join to the letter before them but never to the letter after them: alif, dal, dhal, ra, zay and waw. After one of them, the next letter starts fresh, as if a new word began, even though it is the same word.

steps.note: Alif - does not join forward.
Dal - does not join forward.
Dhal - does not join forward.
Ra - does not join forward.
Zay - does not join forward.
Waw - does not join forward.

steps.question: Which of these does NOT join to the letter after it?
steps.why: Dal never joins forward. Ba and noon do.

steps.question: Which of these does NOT join to the letter after it?
steps.why: Ra never joins forward.

steps.question: How many letters never join forward?
steps.why: Six: alif, dal, dhal, ra, zay and waw.

steps.text: Well walked. Come back to this lesson whenever it feels shaky - Wasia is proud of you.
Assalamu alaikum, my student. When a lam is followed by an alif they are written together as one crossed shape, called lam-alif. It is not a new letter; it is still lam then alif, read 'laa'.

steps.note: Lam-alif: lam then alif, read 'laa'.
With a fatha on the lam: 'laa'.

steps.question: Lam-alif is read as:
steps.why: Lam followed by alif is 'laa'.

steps.question: Is lam-alif a twenty-ninth letter?
options: No, it is lam and alif joined
steps.why: It is lam and alif written together; the alphabet stays twenty-eight letters.

steps.text: Well walked. Come back to this lesson whenever it feels shaky - Wasia is proud of you.
Assalamu alaikum, my student. Look at a whole word. Find the letters from right to left. Remember which ones do not join forward. Then add the marks. Take it slowly; you are reading real Arabic.

steps.note: Seen in the Qur'an at 2:29. Khaa-laam-qaaf, read right to left on the page.
Seen in the Qur'an at 2:187. Kaf, ta, ba, with fathas.
Seen in the Qur'an at 2:22. Jeem, ain, lam, with fathas.
Seen in the Qur'an at 2:102. Kaf, fa, ra, with fathas.

steps.question: In كَتَبَ, which letter comes first (on the right)?
steps.why: Arabic is read right to left; the kaf is first.

steps.question: In جَعَلَ, how many fathas are there?
steps.why: Each of the three letters carries one fatha: ja-'a-la.
